facts.raw_span: A woman in her 30s presented with a painful bruise on her hand
the bruise and pain had persisted despite icing and resting the area
She denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
An ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque was noted on the dorsum of the left hand
Radiography: Showed soft tissue swelling but were otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously hyperintense lesion measuring approximately 1.6 × 0.5 × 2.9 cm
Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
Mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils, histiocytes, and foamy macrophages
Immunohistochemistry: Strongly positive for CD34; negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A
Soft green-blue plaque on the dorsal hand
H&E stain demonstrating spindled cells surrounding fat globules

concepts.why: The presence of a blue-green plaque, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, support the diagnosis of cellular blue nevus.
The initial presentation of a painful bruise on the hand, which persisted despite icing and resting, suggests a hematoma.
The presence of a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on MRI and mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue on pathology support the diagnosis of lipoma.
The presence of a mixed inflammatory infiltrate and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, support the diagnosis of inflammatory pseudotumor.
The history of a twisting injury to the affected hand supports the diagnosis of traumatic injury.
The presence of a blue-green plaque, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate support the diagnosis of PVNS.
The presence of a blue-green plaque and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, support the diagnosis of Nevus of Ota.
The presence of a blue-green plaque, mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate support the diagnosis of malignant melanoma.

rationales.F04: Blue-green plaque is characteristic of cellular blue nevus or pigmented villonodular synovitis
rationales.F06: MRI findings suggest a soft tissue lesion, possibly related to cellular blue nevus or inflammatory pseudotumor
rationales.F08: Spindled cells with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli are characteristic of cellular blue nevus
rationales.F10: Strong positivity for CD34 and negativity for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A support the diagnosis of cellular blue nevus
rationales.F12: H&E stain demonstrating spindled cells surrounding fat globules is consistent with cellular blue nevus
